target_boundary: The current DomainSpec v2 evolvable-validation design, from authored node and edge sources through one causal test receipt, the independent IOLM consumer proof boundary, and the later broader backend-type completeness lane.

reader_contract.target_public: A DomainSpec contributor who knows that specifications describe systems but does not yet know graph admission, obligation derivation, bindings, evaluators, or receipts.
assumed_knowledge: A node represents one authored thing and an edge represents a relationship between two things.
A test compares actual behavior with an expected rule.
reader_contract.reader_reward: The reader can trace one authored relationship into a test result, tell source authority from derived evidence, and identify the exact proof still missing.

must_start_with: Start with the practical promise: an authored relationship should be able to cause a check against a real implementation.
Show the complete proof chain before introducing the component names.
must_not_start_with: Do not begin with algebra or internal type names.
Do not imply that an accepted design review means the test engine is implemented.
opening_contract.failure_message: If the page hides the missing executable predicate or blurs source authority with evidence, it fails the reader contract.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: The authored YAML or JSON that is allowed to state what the domain means.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: Generated code and receipts may explain or test the source, but they may not silently replace it.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: A Markdown explanation, generated graph, or receipt is not automatically source authority.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A named rule set that decides which node kinds and relationship signatures one source set may use.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It lets the language grow through explicit profiles instead of one hard-coded universal union.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Admission says a shape is allowed; it does not prove runtime behavior.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A normalized container of admitted nodes and edges, each tied back to its source and digest.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It gives derivation and checking one stable structure without becoming a second authored truth.
reader_terms.source_or_lane: DEFINE.md candidate contract set; DESIGN.md low-level contracts
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not independently author another semantic graph beside the source graph.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A precise claim that the authored graph requires someone or something to satisfy.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It is the bridge between a relationship in the graph and a check that can be executed.
reader_terms.source_or_lane: DEFINE.md candidate contract set; DESIGN.md derivation interface
reader_terms.misuse_warning: The generator may derive an obligation from authored meaning; it may not invent the meaning.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: An executable check derived from one obligation and an authored formal predicate or fixture.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It turns a specification claim into something a runner can actually evaluate.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: A TestCase must not guess an expected value from prose.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: The explicit mapping from a specification target to a real adapter, implementation, and fixture data.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It proves which implementation was exercised and catches missing adapters or stale digests.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: A binding locates execution; it does not store or invent the expected answer.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A scoped judge that compares evidence against one kind of rule: structural, local, graph, temporal, or semantic.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: Different claims need different checking engines and honest scope labels.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: The evaluator family is a design contract, not proof that all evaluator types exist today.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: An append-only record of what source, binding, execution, evaluator, and verdict produced one result.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It makes a result replayable and auditable without promoting evidence into release authority.
reader_terms.source_or_lane: DEFINE.md candidate contract set; DESIGN.md evidence plane
reader_terms.misuse_warning: A passing receipt is evidence for its declared scope, not universal release approval.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: A named, machine-readable reason why the chain could not continue, such as needs_formal or stale_binding.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: It prevents skips and missing semantics from being counted as success.
reader_terms.source_or_lane: DEFINE.md scope boundary; DESIGN.md workflow failures
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Residue is an honest failure result, not completed proof.

reader_terms.plain_meaning: O_spec is the independently expected obligation set; O_gen is what the engine actually generated.
reader_terms.why_it_matters: Comparing them prevents the generator from grading its own incomplete work as complete.
reader_terms.misuse_warning: Do not use generated obligations as the only oracle for completeness.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a newcomer, I want the promise in ordinary language.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: One authored Rule-enforces-Operation edge should cause a real implementation check and leave a replayable receipt.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: understanding why the architecture exists before learning its parts.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As an implementer, I want to trace one claim end to end.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Source is admitted into a graph, derived into an obligation and TestCase, bound to runtime, judged by an evaluator, and recorded as a receipt.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: finding the exact handoff where proof is absent or corrupted.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As an implementer, I want ownership boundaries between the engine parts.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Source, derivation, execution, and evidence are four planes with explicit digest-bearing handoffs.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: preventing a runner or generator from silently becoming source authority.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a reviewer, I want to know what this design does not own.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: Profiles and relationships own semantic admission; implementations supply runtime behavior; the accepted IOLM lane consumes exact proof handles and emits an independent receipt; Task Session authorizes mutation.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: keeping a bounded engine proof from becoming an inflated product claim.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a planner, I want to see the smallest safe progression.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: L0 proves one causal edge, L1 repeats across a second slice, L2 adds graph laws, and L3 proves all backend kinds and consumers.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: building the framework through distinct decisions instead of a big-bang engine.

layer_reader_outcomes.as_a_reader: As a decision owner, I want the blockers separated from future risks.
layer_reader_outcomes.should_understand: The immediate block is the missing authored formal predicate; closed unions, graph evaluators, and broad consumer completeness come later.
layer_reader_outcomes.because_it_matters_for: choosing the next implementation step without reopening architecture governance.

evidence: DEFINE.md names the target chain Graph, Obligation, TestCase, Binding, Evaluator, and Receipt.
WORK-PACK.md defines success as one Rule --enforces--> Operation path with positive and negative typed receipts.
runs/SWU-GCP-001/TASK-SESSION-RESULT.md records that no implementation mutation or runtime proof has yet occurred.
inference: The clearest newcomer entry is the causal promise, not the internal object vocabulary.

evidence: Invalid node or edge shapes must fail before derivation.
Obligations cite source and rule versions; TestCase cannot invent expected values.
Bindings fail on missing adapters or stale digests.
Receipts separate structural, execution, and evaluator evidence.
Skips, todos, needs_formal, or surviving mutants block completeness.
inference: Digest continuity and an independent negative mutation are the minimum controls for a credible causal receipt.

evidence: NodeSource and EdgeSource carry authored nodes and relationships.
RelationshipSignature admits a typed source-target relationship.
Graph normalizes admitted source without replacing it.
Obligation states a required claim; TestCase makes it runnable; Binding connects it to an implementation.
Evaluator judges a scoped claim; Receipt records the chain and verdict.
inference: These nine contracts form a stable framework seam even while concrete node kinds and evaluator families evolve.

evidence: DESIGN.md separates Source, Derivation, Execution, and Evidence planes.
The workflow is Source -> Normalizer/profile admission -> Deriver -> Binder -> Runner -> Evaluator -> Receipt -> Inventory.
Each handoff is explicit and failures produce typed residue.
IMPLEMENTATION-LAYERING.md keeps graph-law and breadth evaluators outside the first L0 proof.
inference: The strongest architecture property is ownership separation: no single component is allowed to author meaning, execute behavior, and certify itself.

evidence: The relationship registry and selected profile control semantic admission.
Task Session owns bounded execution and stops on missing formal input.
DEC-GCP-002 accepts two independently closable proofs: the executable core and a private IOLM consumption run over its exact handles.
The IOLM machine contract requires a fresh narrow EVF receipt and a separate later BTE breadth rerun; neither consumer verdict changes the upstream core.
The broad backend lane names IOLM, Body War, and Craft as independent consumer proof surfaces.
Node-layering findings require one engine-selected profile, one semantic graph, and generated learner/navigation views keyed by stable IDs.
inference: Consumer receipts are integration evidence, while profile and relationship files remain semantic authority. A missing IOLM receipt blocks only the combined application claim.

evidence: Profile admission accepts or rejects source kinds and edges.
The derivation function maps a normalized graph and rules to ordered obligations while O_spec stays independent.
Test emission returns a TestCase or typed needs_formal residue.
Binding resolves an adapter and implementation digest; evaluator emits a scoped verdict; receipt preserves evidence.
The current key-and-door run stops at TestCase emission because no authored predicate or fixture input exists.
inference: The architecture is compositionally coherent on paper, but graph composability is not proven until the same source digest survives this entire chain and the negative mutation changes the verdict.

evidence: L0 proves one enforces edge through all artifact boundaries plus a negative mutation.
L0C is an independent sibling: after a successful L0 receipt and candidate substrate, IOLM consumes the exact handles and issues a fresh narrow receipt.
L1 adds a second admitted fixture/profile and digest repeatability.
L2 adds bounded reachability, cycle, and closure graph laws with independent receipts.
L3 hands breadth to the backend engine: 13 kinds, 16 signatures, zero skips/todos/orphans/unrunnable cases/surviving mutants, plus independent consumers.
inference: The IOLM consumer lane and backend completeness lane should consume the proven framework seam rather than block the first causal proof.
Immediate blocker: who authors the key-and-door formal predicate and fixture inputs?

Consumer-lane dependency: after the core and candidate substrate pass, can IOLM preserve exact identities, provenance, semantic bytes, and graph/hierarchy/table parity under the versioned machine contract?
After L0: can admitted kinds and signatures evolve without editing closed TypeScript unions?
At L2: what independent oracle judges reachability, cycles, and closure instead of letting the generator grade itself?
At L3: do all 13 kinds and 16 signatures produce independently counted obligations, runnable tests, receipts, and killed mutants?
Across consumers: can IOLM, Body War, and Craft use the same semantic graph without adding shadow authority or view-only pseudo-edges?

evidence: The x-ray library provides node, boundary, layer-panel, risk-marker, arrow, feedback-loop, timeline-strip, risk-matrix, and inspector-rail primitives.
The dependency-boundary, lifecycle-stack, and evidence-inference-split patterns cover the principal layout needs.
L0 static HTML/SVG supports a local inspectable artifact with no remote renderer dependency.
inference: A local unpromoted pattern named pattern.proof-chain-spine best exposes digest-bearing handoffs and the exact stop point; consider promotion only after another real architecture reuses it.

evidence_boundary.source_backed: Candidate architecture and accepted planning/review artifacts are source-backed.
evidence_boundary.not_proven: No end-to-end executable receipt or independent IOLM consumer receipt exists; S1, the combined application claim, and the backend completeness exit remain blocked.
evidence_boundary.current_decision: DEC-GCP-001 is pending; DEC-GCP-002 is accepted as a two-proof chain with independent core and IOLM receipts.
evidence_boundary.consumer_blocker: IOLM 00C-B has an accepted upstream-support route but no passing cross-feature-support receipt; therefore the candidate-substrate handle and both IOLM consumer receipts remain unavailable without blocking EVF core closure.
